content:
Dear Hiring Team at Halden Pay,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. Over nine years, I have built and operated production data platforms and cloud warehouses across logistics, e-commerce and payments. Halden Pay’s focus on a shared platform for product, analytics and data science teams is a strong match for the work I do: building reliable, reusable data systems that help teams make good use of trusted data.

At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration across a platform with around 140 Airflow DAGs, and I migrated warehouse transformations to more than 420 tested and documented dbt models. That work reduced the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I have also introduced data contracts with JSON Schema and CI checks, and built a Kafka-based shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day. These projects have involved day-to-day platform ownership, data quality, SQL and warehouse optimization, and working across teams to make pipelines more dependable.

My experience in payments is directly relevant to Halden Pay. At Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers, processing about 1.2 TB of raw files daily. The work reduced month-end manual reconciliation from around three days to four hours. I also designed a Redshift star-schema warehouse for finance and risk teams and established Great Expectations checks for critical finance tables. Alongside hands-on AWS experience, I hold the AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate certification.

I value clear data contracts, well-tested pipelines and open-source collaboration. I have contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider, and I would welcome the opportunity to bring this practical, ownership-focused approach to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team and help build foundations that move quickly without sacrificing reliability. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could contribute.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise cover letter with a clear senior-level narrative. It establishes relevant platform experience, uses quantified outcomes effectively, connects prior payments experience to Halden Pay, and maintains a professional tone. The progression from platform ownership to payments-domain relevance is logical and credible. The main content limitation is that Python, SQL optimization, and broader data-modelling capability are not surfaced as explicitly as the job description requests. The closing is polite but somewhat generic; it could reinforce the specific value Lena would bring to a shared Data Platform team.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard text, conventional paragraphs, no tables or graphics, and includes several relevant keywords such as Senior Data Engineer, data platforms, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, JSON Schema, CI checks, PySpark, AWS EMR, Redshift, Great Expectations, data quality, and open-source. AI screening probability is high because the document contains strong quantified evidence and directly matches the role title and payments domain. ATS alignment would improve if the letter explicitly used supported terms from the advertisement, including Python, SQL optimization/query optimization, dimensional modelling, production data platform operations, reusable frameworks, and data quality standards.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns very well with the core role: it demonstrates production data-platform ownership, cloud warehouse experience at scale, Airflow and dbt, streaming and batch processing, data quality, payments experience, open-source contribution, and professional English. AWS is a credible comparable cloud to Google Cloud, and this is presented clearly through AWS EMR and related data-platform work. The candidate also aligns with Ownership and Pace through quantified reliability, runtime, and reconciliation improvements, and with collaborative working through data contracts and open-source contribution. The document does not show graph modelling or Portuguese; these are gaps in the candidate material rather than defects in the letter. It also does not explicitly demonstrate every aspect of governance, access policies, or collaboration with data scientists, although the documented data-contract and data-quality work is relevant adjacent evidence.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR / HIGH-VALUE ATS AND ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, explicitly name Python and SQL optimization using evidence already present in the candidate material. For example, revise the sentence beginning "These projects have involved" to: "These projects have involved day-to-day production data-platform ownership, advanced Python and SQL work, query and warehouse optimization, data quality, and collaboration across product and data teams." Only use this wording if "advanced" accurately reflects the candidate's level; otherwise write "substantial Python and SQL work."
2. In the third paragraph, add the supported Python-library experience after the Redshift sentence to strengthen the Python requirement. For example: "I also wrote an internal Python library for S3 and the Glue Data Catalog that was adopted by four teams." This is more direct evidence than relying only on PySpark.
3. In the second paragraph, make the data-modelling evidence more explicit by changing "These projects have involved..." or the surrounding sentence to include "dimensional modelling." A supported version is: "I have also worked with dimensional modelling, including a Redshift star-schema warehouse with more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams." This could be added to the payments paragraph if space permits.
4. In the final paragraph, replace the generic phrase "bring this practical, ownership-focused approach" with a more role-specific version that uses the advertisement's terminology: "bring this practical, ownership-focused approach to Halden Pay's shared Data Platform, building reusable and well-tested foundations for analytics, product, and data teams." This accurately reflects the candidate's platform, testing, data-contract, and cross-team experience without claiming unsupported data-science collaboration.
5. Keep the final letter to approximately its current length. Do not add unsupported claims about Google Cloud, graph modelling, Portuguese, GKE, Cloud Run, or access-policy ownership.

content:
Dear Hiring Team at Halden Pay,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. Over nine years, I have built and operated production data platforms and cloud warehouses across logistics, e-commerce and payments. Halden Pay’s focus on a shared platform for product, analytics and data science teams is a strong match for the work I do: building reliable, reusable data systems that help teams make good use of trusted data.

At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration across a platform with around 140 Airflow DAGs, and I migrated warehouse transformations to more than 420 tested dbt models. That work reduced the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 50 minutes. I have also introduced data contracts with JSON Schema and CI checks, and built a Kafka-based shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day. I also reduced Snowflake spend from approximately 38k to 24k per month through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables. Together, these projects demonstrate my experience designing, building and operating a production data platform; using advanced Python and SQL for large-scale data processing and query optimisation; and implementing data quality controls and reusable platform foundations.

My experience in payments is directly relevant to Halden Pay. At Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers, processing about 1.2 TB of raw files daily. The work reduced month-end manual reconciliation from around three days to four hours. I also designed a Redshift star-schema warehouse, applying dimensional modelling across more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams. I also wrote an internal Python library for S3 and the Glue Data Catalog that was adopted by four teams, and established Great Expectations checks for critical finance tables. Alongside hands-on AWS experience with S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM and Docker-based engineering workflows, I hold the AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate certification.

I value clear data contracts, well-tested pipelines and open-source collaboration. I am particularly interested in building reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines. I have applied this approach through shared data contracts, tested dbt models, CDC and replay tooling, and internal Python libraries used by multiple teams. I have contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider, and I would welcome the opportunity to bring this practical, ownership-focused approach to Halden Pay’s shared Data Platform, building reusable and well-tested foundations in collaboration with product teams and data users. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could contribute.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm
